rationales: Air is generally treated as a homogeneous mixture of gases.
Rock is a heterogeneous mixture of different minerals.
Gasoline is generally treated as a homogeneous mixture.
Ice cream is a colloidal, heterogeneous mixture, so this question has more than one correct option.
HO does not give glucose’s simplest whole-number atom ratio.
CH has the wrong carbon-to-hydrogen ratio for glucose.
CH₂O is the simplest formula obtained by reducing C₆H₁₂O₆.
H₂O₂ is not the empirical formula of glucose.
C-12 is a stable carbon isotope, not the isotope used for this treatment.
C-14 is chiefly used for radiocarbon dating.
P-32 is used in the treatment of skin cancer.
I-131 is mainly used for thyroid disorders.
The second and third periods are called short periods.
Normal periods is not the name for the second and third periods.
Long periods refers to the fourth and fifth periods.
Very long periods refers to the sixth and seventh periods.
A covalent bond forms when atoms share electrons.
Donation of electrons alone describes electron transfer, not covalent bonding.
Acceptance of electrons alone describes electron transfer, not covalent bonding.
Repulsion of electrons does not form a covalent bond.
CH₄ is nonpolar and poorly soluble in water.
C₂H₂ is only slightly soluble in water.
NaCl dissolves readily in water.
C₆H₆ is nonpolar and does not dissolve readily in water.
Manufacturing sulphuric acid is an application of industrial chemistry.
Biochemistry studies chemical processes in living organisms.
Organic chemistry focuses mainly on carbon compounds.
Inorganic chemistry studies inorganic substances, but not their industrial manufacture as such.
Sugar is a compound, not a mixture.
Water is a compound, not a mixture.
Oxygen is an element, not a mixture.
Air is a mixture of gases.
Deuterium has mass number 2 and atomic number 1, so it has one neutron.
One neutron is the number in deuterium.
Two neutrons would make the mass number 3 for hydrogen.
Three neutrons would make the mass number 4 for hydrogen.
Li is farther left in the period and has a larger atomic radius.
Be has a larger atomic radius than elements farther to its right in the period.
Ne is taken as the smallest by the simple left-to-right periodic trend used here.
F is slightly to the left of Ne in the period and is not the expected smallest by that trend.
NaNO₃ becomes more soluble as temperature increases.
Li₂SO₄ has decreasing solubility as temperature rises.
Ce₂(SO₄)₃ becomes less soluble as temperature increases.
NaCl solubility changes only slightly with temperature.
Water is the strongly polar solvent conventionally used to dissolve polar covalent compounds.
Benzene is nonpolar and is not the expected solvent for polar compounds.
Ether is less polar than water and is not the standard answer here.
Acetone is polar, but water is the conventional solvent matched to this rule.
NaCl is primarily ionic and has no coordinate covalent bond.
NH₄Cl contains an ammonium ion formed by donation of a nitrogen lone pair to H⁺.
H₂O has ordinary covalent O–H bonds.
NH₃ has ordinary covalent N–H bonds and a lone pair, but no coordinate bond in the molecule.
C₁₀H₂₂ has stronger intermolecular attractions and evaporates more slowly.
C₉H₂₀ evaporates more slowly than the shorter-chain alkanes listed.
C₈H₁₈ is less volatile than C₆H₁₄.
C₆H₁₄ has the lowest boiling point among these and evaporates most rapidly.
15.2°C is not tin’s transition temperature.
14.2°C is not tin’s transition temperature.
Tin’s transition temperature is 13.2°C.
12.2°C is not tin’s transition temperature.
